target.title: fix: pre-update config snapshot blocked after transient read errors
target.body:
Closes #105431

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running an OpenClaw update would permanently lose the pre-update config backup for that process when the first snapshot attempt hit a transient read/write failure (disk pressure, file lock, etc.). Later update writes then skipped snapshotting even though no `.pre-update` file existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` marked a config path as snapshotted before the best-effort read/write completed. That permanently blocked retries after transient IO errors. The tracker now records success only after the snapshot write completes, while still keeping the once-per-process skip after a successful snapshot.

## User Impact

Update flows can recover a pre-update config backup after a transient snapshot failure instead of silently proceeding without one for the rest of the process.

## Evidence

- Focused local tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/config.backup-rotation.test.ts` → 9 passed (includes new `retries after a transient read failure` case)
- Crabbox/Testbox warmup unavailable in this environment (`crabbox` binary sanity check failed); CI will cover remote proof
- Autoreview helper could not run (`codex` executable not installed); change is a 2-file tracker ordering fix with sibling test coverage
